summary: Extends IPv6 Neighbor Discovery so a node can ask for the IPv6 address that matches a known link-layer address. This is the inverse of the usual lookup, which finds a link-layer address from an IP address.

eli5.summary: Normally you know someone's name and look for their house. This lets you know the house and ask who lives there.

subtitle: How an IPv6 node that knows a neighbor's link-layer address can ask for that neighbor's IPv6 addresses.

tldr.problem: IPv6 Neighbor Discovery finds a link-layer address from an IPv6 address. On networks such as Frame Relay, a node can know the link-layer identifier of a remote node but not its IPv6 addresses.
tldr.mechanism: Inverse Neighbor Discovery (IND) adds two ICMPv6 messages, a Solicitation (type 141) and an Advertisement (type 142), plus Source and Target Address List options. The solicitation goes to a known link-layer address and the advertisement returns the IPv6 addresses of that interface.
tldr.outcome: A node can learn the IPv6 addresses behind a known link-layer address, and optionally cache the mapping. The RFC was developed for Frame Relay but may apply to other networks with similar behavior.

today: RFC 3122 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its original target was Frame Relay networks, and it may apply to other networks with similar behavior.

sections.title: The Inverse of Neighbor Discovery
sections.content:
IPv6 Neighbor Discovery (ND) is how a node learns the link-layer address that goes with an IPv6 address. Inverse Neighbor Discovery (IND) runs the other way. A node that knows the link-layer address of a directly connected remote node learns that node's IPv6 addresses.

It does this by sending solicitations and receiving advertisements that carry one or more IPv6 addresses for the known link-layer address. IND was originally developed for Frame Relay networks but may also apply to other networks with similar behavior.

The RFC notes similarities and differences with Inverse ARP for IPv4 (RFC 2390) or its replacement documents.
sections.eli5: Usually you have an address and look for the mailbox. Here you already have the mailbox and want to learn the names of the people who use it.

sections.title: The Solicitation and Advertisement Messages
sections.content:
Both messages are ICMPv6 messages with the same layout: Type, Code, Checksum, a 32-bit Reserved field and then options. Reserved MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored by the receiver.

The Solicitation is ICMPv6 type 141, code 0. The sender does not know the target's IPv6 address, so the destination is the all-nodes link-scope multicast address FF02::1. At the link layer, though, it goes directly to the target node by its known link-layer address. The Hop Limit is 255. The source is an address of the sending interface. If an IP Authentication Header security association exists, the sender SHOULD include that header. The message MUST carry the Source Link-Layer Address and Target Link-Layer Address options, and MAY carry a Source Address List and an MTU option.

The Advertisement is type 142, code 0, Hop Limit 255, and is sent to the source address of the solicitation. It MUST carry the Source Link-Layer Address, the Target Link-Layer Address and a Target Address List, and MAY carry an MTU option.

Receivers MUST silently ignore options they do not recognize and continue processing.
sections.eli5: You send a note to one specific mailbox, saying who you are. The reply lists everyone who lives at that mailbox.

sections.title: The Address List Options
sections.content:
IND defines two options: the Source Address List (type 9) and the Target Address List (type 10). Both have a type, a length, a reserved field and one or more 128-bit IPv6 addresses. The Length is counted in units of 8 octets, including the Type, Length and Reserved fields. The minimum is 3, which holds one address. The number of addresses is n = (Length - 1)/2.

The Source Address List lists addresses of the interface named by the Source Link-Layer Address. It MUST fit in one solicitation, so it may be incomplete. The sender should rely on the advertisement for a full list. The Target Address List SHOULD be the complete list for the interface named by the Target Link-Layer Address. If it does not fit in one advertisement, further advertisements SHOULD carry the rest.

The mechanism only provides address mapping information. It does not say how returned addresses are used, and it does not exclude any kind of address, such as manually configured, autoconfigured, temporary, unicast or multicast ones. An implementation MUST NOT send duplicates in the list.
sections.eli5: The reply is a list of names. If the list is too long for one page, it continues on the next page, and nobody is listed twice.

sections.title: How Senders and Receivers Behave
sections.content:
IND works much like ND. The soliciting node sends a solicitation and the target answers with an advertisement. What is learned MAY be stored in the Neighbor Discovery cache.

Sender. The sender SHOULD retransmit about every RetransTimer while waiting, rate-limited to at most one solicitation per neighbor per RetransTimer. If no advertisement arrives after MAX_MULTICAST_SOLICIT solicitations, inverse address resolution has failed, and if an upper layer required it, the sender MUST tell that layer about the error.

Receiver of a solicitation. It SHOULD send an advertisement, and SHOULD put the sender's address and link-layer address mapping into its ND cache as it would for an ND solicitation. It SHOULD return one or more addresses of the interface in the Target Address List, without duplicates.

Receiver of an advertisement. It SHOULD put the mapping from the Target Address List and the Source Link-Layer Address into its ND cache, as for an ND advertisement.
sections.eli5: If nobody answers after a few tries, you give up and tell whoever asked. If someone answers, you write the answer in your address book.

sections.title: Message Validation
sections.content:
A node MUST silently discard a solicitation unless the Hop Limit is 255, any Authentication Header verifies, the ICMP checksum is valid, the code is 0, the ICMP length is 24 or more octets, both required link-layer address options are present, and every option has a length greater than zero.

An advertisement is checked the same way, except the ICMP length must be 48 or more octets, and the Source Link-Layer Address, Target Link-Layer Address and Target Address List options must all be present, with the Target Address List length at least 3.

Reserved fields and unrecognized options MUST be ignored. The only defined option besides the required ones is MTU. Other ND options not specified for IND messages are ignored and the packet is processed as normal.
sections.eli5: Mail that does not follow the rules gets thrown away without a word, so troublemakers get no reply.

sections.title: Use on Frame Relay Networks
sections.content:
Appendix A explains the original use case. In Frame Relay, each virtual circuit is identified at a node by a Data Link Connection Identifier (DLCI), which serves as the remote node's link-layer address. The network tells a node its own DLCI for a circuit but not the DLCI the remote end uses for it, and it carries no IPv6 addresses. IND finds both.

In the RFC's example, node A identifies the circuit to node B as DLCI 30, while B identifies it to A as DLCI 62. A sends a solicitation with Target DLCI 30. The receiver replaces the Source Link-Layer Address with the DLCI from the Frame Relay header, so B sees Source DLCI 62 and Target DLCI 30. B's advertisement swaps them: Source 30, Target 62, plus its addresses.

Both addresses use the Q.922 DLCI format, with 10 significant bits by default or 23. A receiver may use the MTU option to set a better MTU for the circuit. The receiver of an advertisement MAY store the Target address as the DLCI at the remote end, and MAY pair its own local addresses with the target's addresses, for example by shared prefix.
sections.eli5: Two friends each give the same phone line a different nickname. This process lets each friend find out what the other calls it, and who is on the other end.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
On point-to-point virtual circuits, such as Frame Relay, IND messages are less exposed to impersonation by on-link nodes than on broadcast links. As in ND, off-link senders are ignored by checking that the Hop Limit is 255, since routers decrement it and a packet with 255 must have come from a neighbor.

IND exchanges can be authenticated with the IP Authentication Header. A node SHOULD include it when a security association exists, and received headers MUST be verified, with incorrect ones ignored. It SHOULD be possible to configure a node to ignore unauthenticated IND messages, but that switch SHOULD default to allowing them. For Frame Relay, the DLCI preprocessing MUST happen after IP Security processing. Confidentiality is left to the IP Security documents.
sections.eli5: Notes from far away are ignored because the stamp shows they came too far. You can also require a signed seal on every note if you want.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA was asked to assign two ICMPv6 type values from the Informational range, one for each message, with no code values other than 0. Future code assignments are to be made under Standards Action. IANA was also asked to assign two ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery option types for the Address List options.
sections.eli5: The official list of message numbers got two new entries, one for asking and one for answering.
